documents.title: Missed appointment 01/20
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Bryant, we missed you at your diabetes visit yesterday morning (01/20). Please reply or text us with a few dates that work and we will get you back on the schedule. Your yearly FIT kit is also due; we can mail one to your home.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment 01/20
documents.author: patient
documents.body: sorry about that. got held over in Wyoming with the storm and couldn't get back. I'm running West most of the winter. mail me the kit and I'll do it when I'm home. I'll call about the appt when I know my schedule

documents.title: FIT kit mailed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: FIT kit mailed to home address with return envelope and instructions. Front desk will keep reaching out to reschedule the diabetes visit.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mailed FIT returned, collected 03/16. Negative. Patient notified. Reminded him he is overdue for his diabetes visit and labs; he says he will book once his spring routes are set.

documents.title: Mail-order renewals
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Mail-order renewal requests for all five chronic medications (metformin 1000 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg).
Last diabetes visit 07/2025; missed 01/20/2026 visit. Per PCP: approve one 90-day supply, front desk to book a visit with labs.
Front desk reached patient: booked 07/21/2026 at 8:00, fasting.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 62-year-old here fasting; first diabetes visit in a year after missing the January appointment (snowed in out West). Says the winter on the road was hard on his eating: drive-thru most days, energy drinks. Evening metformin missed "more than I want to admit." Morning medicines daily. No chest pain, dyspnea, foot sores. Walking and swallowing unchanged. Eye exam still not done.

Problems: T2DM (2004), HTN, HLD, obesity, OSA, achalasia, cervical spondylotic myelopathy, former smoker.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
NKDA.

O: BP 144/87, HR 59, RR 16, T 36.5, SpO2 95%. Wt 101.6 kg, BMI 32.0.
No distress. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Gait unsteady as before. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament normal.

A/P:
1. T2DM: A1c, BMP, urine albumin/creatinine and lipids today. Long talk about the energy drinks and the missed evening dose; he will set an alarm and keep metformin in the cab. Results by portal; diabetes visit in 3 months.
2. HTN: 144/87 today, home readings 130s per patient. Continue.
3. HLD: continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Lung cancer screening: he passed 15 years since quitting (03/2011) in 03/2026. Screening ends; no further LDCT.
5. Eye exam: reminder still open; optometry number again.
6. Colorectal: FIT negative 03/2026.
Next visit 10/20.

documents.title: Labs 07/21
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
A1c 9.2 (7.9 a year ago). Glucose 193 fasting. Creatinine 0.99, eGFR 86, K 4.4. Urine albumin/creatinine 11. TC 215, HDL 35, TG 234, LDL 133.
Portal message to patient: A1c is well above where it has been. Same plan as at the visit - metformin twice every day, cut out energy drinks and soda, packed meals. Recheck at the 10/20 visit.

documents.title: RE: Labs 07/21
documents.author: patient
documents.body: yeah I figured. no more energy drinks starting now. see you in October

events.reason: Sudden painless vision loss, right eye

documents.title: Emergency department provider note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN NOTE (copy to primary care)
Date of visit: 08/04/2026
Patient: Lamar Bryant, 62-year-old man, DOB 02/26/1964

Chief complaint: vision loss, right eye.

HPI: Earlier today, while home, the vision in his right eye dropped off suddenly. No pain. He describes dark specks drifting across the vision of that eye. No eye trauma, no headache, no flashes described. Left eye normal. He has type 2 diabetes that has been poorly controlled, with a recent hemoglobin A1c of 9.2%. Also hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Social: long-haul truck driver. Former smoker, 20 pack-years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Vital signs: BP 145/90, HR 78, RR 16.

Eye examination:
Visual acuity: right 20/200, left 20/25.
Right eye: red reflex absent. Dark strands visible within the vitreous.
Left eye: fundus unremarkable.
Extraocular movements full. Conjunctivae not injected.

Bedside ocular ultrasound, right eye: vitreous hemorrhage. Retina attached; no retinal detachment or tear seen.

ED course: findings discussed with on-call ophthalmology, who will see him in clinic tomorrow morning.

Diagnosis: Vitreous hemorrhage, right eye.

Disposition: Discharged home from the ED. Ophthalmology appointment 08/05/2026 in the morning. Return for eye pain, worsening vision, or a curtain or shadow over the vision. Not to drive; wife driving him.
